T1.desc: catalog chi, orientability, holes/twists match the classification
T1.detail: sphere chi=2; projective plane chi=1; torus chi=0; Klein bottle chi=0; genus-2 surface chi=-2; genus-3 surface chi=-4; Dyck's surface chi=-1

T2.desc: connected sum: Euler genus adds and orientable iff both; T # RP2 matches RP2#RP2#RP2 (Dyck)

T3.desc: Gauss-Bonnet: each gluing polygon fits curvature of the sign of chi, and only that sign
T3.detail: sphere: 4-gon angle 270deg, curvature positive; projective plane: 4-gon angle 180deg, curvature positive; torus: 4-gon angle 90deg, curvature flat; Klein bottle: 4-gon angle 90deg, curvature flat; genus-2 surface: 8-gon angle 45deg, curvature negative; genus-3 surface: 12-gon angle 30deg, curvature negative; Dyck's surface: 6-gon angle 60deg, curvature negative

T4.desc: drawn genus-g surfaces have mesh chi = 2 - 2g

T5.desc: every convex shape is one type: solid chi 1, surface chi 2 (5 solids x p in 1,2,5,inf; 3 depth mixes)

T6.desc: p does not change topology: lp torus chi = 0 at every p; round torus total curvature = 0

T7.desc: aspect ratio R/r: ring (R>r) has a hole, spindle (R<r) has none; the change is at the horn R = r
T7.detail: R/r=2.0: surface chi 0, solid chi 0; R/r=1.4: surface chi 0, solid chi 0; R/r=1.1: surface chi 0, solid chi 0; R/r=0.9: surface chi 2, solid chi 1; R/r=0.6: surface chi 2, solid chi 1; R/r=0.3: surface chi 2, solid chi 1

T8.desc: chi multiplies on products (f-vectors convolve, t=-1 reading), so 1-chi composes as x+y-xy
T8.detail: circle x circle chi = 0, S2 x S2 chi = 4

T9.desc: Clifford torus (p=2 circles x circles in R4) sits on the unit 3-sphere with a constant (flat) metric
